newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end flat, outperform on S&P upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end flat, outperform on S&P upgrade.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended little changed on Monday but climbed off early lows to outperform U.S. Treasuries after Standard & Poor's upgraded Canada's foreign currency debt rating outlook, analysts said.

"That helped us turn the corner," said a bond trader with one bank-owned brokerage. "We opened up a lot weaker to the U.S. As we started trading we tightened into them. Basically it's very, very quiet," he said.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.03 to C$112.95 to yield 6.922 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 6/32 to yield 6.65 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 27 basis points from 28 basis points at Friday's close.

"The market was weaker to begin with. There was rumoured selling of both 10 years and long bonds in the market on an overnight basis," said a second bond trader. "The market started to rally after the S&P upgrade," he said.

S&P said earlier on Monday it upgraded Canada's foreign currency debt rating outlook because falling government deficits have put the country on a better financial footing. However, Canada still has too much debt to be reassigned the triple-A rating it lost in 1992, the debt rating agency said.

New York-based S&P upgraded the outlook on Canada's foreign currency rating to stable from negative. The agency also confirmed the foreign currency debt rating at AA+ and the local currency rating at AAA.

Analysts said activity was subdued in the Canadian market with many players sidelined until U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivers his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday and Thursday. Many investors are expecting Greenspan to offer hints about the near-term direction of U.S. rates.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.10 to C$105.40 to yield 6.251 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 13 basis points from 11 basis points on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.88 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.11 percent.
